title: runtime/kv-cache: refactor compaction counters + add per-request cache state annotations
author: Omar El-Sayed
description:
Context: For the Q1'26 perf baseline suite we need to explain TTFT/TPOT + tail latency shifts in workloads where KV cache pressure drives compaction/eviction. Today we have a single bucketed counter (kv_cache_compaction_total) that conflates: (a) compaction attempts, (b) work performed, and (c) outcome (reclaim success vs no-op). Also, benchmark runs/dashboards currently can't correlate outliers to cache behavior at the request level (hit/miss/partial + eviction during decode).

What this PR does:
- Refactors KV cache compaction metrics into explicit counters + bytes moved and time spent; removes the ambiguous "compaction_total" counter from the hot path.
- Adds per-request cache state annotations emitted on the request trace span and (when enabled) attached to benchmark artifacts. This is intended for baseline analysis and variance investigations (no prompt/token content is included).
- Adds a lightweight, cardinality-safe enum and sampling gate. Default sampling is off in production; enabled in perf-canary/benchmark runner.

New metrics (runtime scope):
- kv_cache.compaction_attempt_total{reason}
- kv_cache.compaction_success_total{reason}
- kv_cache.compaction_noop_total{reason}
- kv_cache.compaction_bytes_moved_total
- kv_cache.compaction_pages_reclaimed_total
- kv_cache.compaction_duration_ms_total

New request annotation fields (trace + optional benchmark JSON):
- kv_cache_state: HIT | PARTIAL | MISS
- kv_cache_evicted_during_decode: true|false
- kv_cache_reused_prefix_tokens: int (bucketed when emitted to metrics; raw only in benchmark artifacts)
- kv_cache_effective_prefix_ratio: float (0..1, benchmark artifacts only)

Notes on overhead/correctness:
- Counters are bumped at compaction boundary, not per token.
- Request annotations are added at finalize() time from existing cache bookkeeping (no additional locks); sampling gate prevents high-volume export.

Rollout:
- Production: metrics on; request annotations off by default.
- Perf-canary + benchmark suite: annotations on (1.0 sampling) to support baseline explainability.

Testing:
- Added unit tests for compaction reason classification and noop vs success.
- Added integration test in runtime_bench harness validating that request annotation schema is present when flag is enabled.

Docs:
- Updated internal metrics registry notes for KV cache (links in code comments).

Follow-ups:
- I did not rename existing dashboards here; Observability will pick up new metric names in the baseline dashboard spec update. Existing metric kv_cache_compaction_total remains exported for one release behind a deprecated alias to avoid breaking current queries.
commits: kv-cache: split compaction metrics into attempt/success/noop + bytes/duration
kv-cache: plumb per-request cache state into request context
telemetry: add trace span attributes for cache state (gated + sampled)
bench: optionally export request cache annotations in run artifacts
tests: compaction outcome classification + benchmark schema validation
docs: note deprecation path for kv_cache_compaction_total
files_changed: runtime/telemetry/flags.h (kv cache annotation flags + sampling knobs)
conversation:
Samir Qureshi (review): Can we confirm we're not incrementing these counters per-page in the hot loop? Also, I want to make sure 'noop' is not masking a bug where we early return due to lock contention.
Omar El-Sayed (author): Counters are only incremented once per compaction invocation; bytes/pages are accumulated from the compaction summary struct, not per-page. Re: noop: it's only emitted when (a) candidate set empty OR (b) computed reclaimable pages == 0. Lock contention path still emits attempt_total{reason="..."} + noop_total{reason="lock_unavailable"} (added in latest push).

Thomas Baird (review): Please be very careful with per-request fields. Anything with raw token counts can explode cardinality if it hits metrics. I'd like an explicit guarantee in code that raw values only go to artifacts and not to metrics.
Omar El-Sayed (author): Agreed. I split the exports: trace attributes are enum/bool only; metrics export is strictly counters + totals. The raw int/ratio fields are only written into benchmark artifact JSON when runtime_bench.enable_request_annotations=true. Added a static_assert in the metrics exporter to prevent adding numeric per-request dimensions.

Logan Wright (review): For traces, does adding these attributes require touching the span on the decode thread? If so, any contention? Also, can you name the attributes with our standard prefix (kv_cache.*)?
Omar El-Sayed (author): Attributes are attached at request finalize on the request context thread (same place we already set model/version and token counts). Renamed to kv_cache.state and kv_cache.evicted_during_decode per your suggestion in 2/19 push.

Nadia Rahman (review): I'm worried about HIT vs PARTIAL definition. Is PARTIAL based on prefix reuse tokens > 0, or on whether we had to recompute any prefix? Please define precisely; baseline analysis will depend on it.
Omar El-Sayed (author): Updated definition in code comments + test: HIT = reused_prefix_tokens == prompt_tokens (full prefix reuse), PARTIAL = 0 < reused_prefix_tokens < prompt_tokens, MISS = reused_prefix_tokens == 0. Also added kv_cache.evicted_during_decode when we detect a cache line dropped after prefill (this was the case we saw in the long-context streaming outliers).

Marcus Reed (review): Bench artifacts: can we keep the schema backward compatible? Existing parsers in perf-canary expect a stable top-level shape.
Omar El-Sayed (author): Kept backward compat by adding an optional block request_annotations[]. Top-level remains unchanged; if flag disabled, field is omitted. Added a parser fixture in runtime/bench/tests to ensure older readers don't crash (they ignore unknown fields).

Sean Gallagher (review): Any chance this changes behavior under memory pressure? I want to avoid a 'metrics refactor' subtly shifting compaction thresholds.
Omar El-Sayed (author): No policy changes. Compaction thresholds/triggering remain identical; I only moved the counter increments to a single post-compaction summary function and improved reason labeling. Verified perf smoke: within noise for steady-state; run-to-run variance improved in our baseline debug job because we can now segment on cache_state.
ci_checks: perf-canary/perf-smoke (non-blocking): PASS (rerun after 1st attempt failed due to runner capacity)
release_notes: Runtime telemetry: KV cache compaction metrics are now split into explicit attempt/success/noop counters + bytes/duration. Added optional per-request KV cache state annotations for baseline/perf-canary analysis (disabled by default in production). Deprecated alias for kv_cache_compaction_total retained for one release.
